item.title: First shapes of my mighty pirate
item.description: Second drawing. Starting from different references for pose, subject and details, I blocked in the first basic shapes of my mighty pirate.

item.title: Jim is done
item.description: Jim’s finished. The more I look at it the more flaws I see, but it doesn’t matter — it’s already time to think about the next drawing: the mighty pirate.

item.title: Guybrush
item.description: Back again — and I’ve already broken my promise to draw more during the week. Here’s a quick sketch of how Guybrush from Monkey Island might look, the one I want to tackle after my Jim Carrey. The tricky part will be that I have no real reference photo to copy the features and shading from.

item.title: Fat people & hands
item.description: I squeezed in some drawing practice during a work-from-home break, focusing on fat people and hands to push myself out of my comfort zone with less standard proportions. I learned how important the double chin is, and how key it is to nail the basic geometric shapes inside the subject first.

item.title: Progress on my Jim Carrey portrait
item.description: Second class. I reworked the Jim Carrey — fixing the too-close eyes and the too-narrow lower face — then finally started shading, building from a light base up to darker layers. I’ll probably finish it next class, but that’s at least two frustrating weeks away.

item.title: Drawing with Guybrush Threepwood
item.description: I’m realizing I need a clear subject to feel motivated. My next real project will be Guybrush Threepwood, a character from a ’90s pirate adventure game with a touch of voodoo. So while I finish the Jim Carrey, I’ll spend some sessions studying pirate clothing and weird voodoo items.

item.title: What a grind
item.description: Since I said I wanted to get back to properly mastering drawing like I used to, I signed up for a drawing course and decided to start with a black-and-white copy of a face. God, what a grind.
